leads.work: Daily emails telling the real-time desk about short and long positions and lending (EPE lending at Palo Verde, SP-15, Mid-C), with deal numbers and prices, so shift traders can fill or sell the positions in Enpower
leads.why: Bill Williams and Kate Symes send near-daily hand-typed notices about each day's length or shortness and lending, often adding 'check with X on price'. The same information already sits in the trading books and could be generated as a report.

leads.work: El Paso Electric (EPE) reconciliation: tying the El Paso model to the CARP report, logging totals in the reconciliation model, settling disputes, requesting and listening to call tapes, and sending repeated reminders about unit dispatch rules
leads.why: One month's checkout took five days (the next took five minutes). Disputes with EPE and other Southwest counterparties are 'growing', Kate requests 'several sets of tapes' to settle them, and there are repeated all-caps reminders about not selling below $15 without ramping down Four Corners. The work is manual, error-prone and recurs every month.

leads.work: Manual 10-step procedure for handling Colstrip cuts in Enpower, deal scheduling, Lotus Notes cuts database, discussion forum and email
leads.why: A written step-by-step procedure that is repeated every time Colstrip goes down. Bill calls the Lotus Notes cuts database entry 'the most time consuming portion of this procedure', and 'Cuts (yet again)' is on a meeting agenda.

leads.work: Daily emails reporting CAISO congestion relief revenue to Volume Management and Risk, checking it against the California flash, tracking exposure in a spreadsheet, and the month-end ISO true-up
leads.why: Bill emails the MW, price and revenue to Jim Reyes and others nearly every day. Murray O'Neil asks for daily contact to keep a net payable position. Revenue goes missing from the flash, and the month-end true-up leaves variances to chase by hand.

leads.work: Enpower vs CAPS variance reports and interdesk book transfers: entering extra deals only to make a report come out flat, fixing SAR variances, and building book-to-book transfer deals
leads.why: Bill says he adds deals that are 'only necessary for the sake of the report' and would prefer not to. Interdesk sales have to be routed by hand, and traders send in transfer deal numbers.

leads.work: Hourly deal entry and inc sheet upkeep after EnronOnline (EOL) hourly launch: entering and routing deals every hour, a night-shift weighted-average interdesk strip, and repeated process memos
leads.why: Volume rose sharply (530+ trades in 8 days). Systems and staff were not ready, EOL trades were missed, and Bill keeps re-issuing deal-entry standards and reminders. This is a strong candidate for automated deal capture and booking.

leads.work: Matching Bloomberg broker deals to Enpower and assigning broker fees
leads.why: Evelyn Metoyer's spreadsheet lists unmatched Bloomberg deals for August 1–22, past the agreed two-day grace period. The $15 flat fee per trade is entered by hand per deal and gets misapplied.

leads.work: Setting up the new EOL hourly products: loadshape language reviewed by legal, pop-up announcement text, and a website filter request
leads.why: The product setup goes through several hand-offs, and emails meant for Bill are sent to the wrong Bill Williams.

leads.work: Mail misrouted between people with the same name (Bill Williams / Bill Williams III) and wrong distribution lists, each needing a reply or forward
leads.why: About ten instances in this batch alone: badge access requests, baby shower notices, the admin assistant list, a DS-3 quote and EOL requests. Each one costs both sides time to bounce back.

leads.work: Controlling cell phone costs: overage reminders, per-employee caps and billing back, and plan changes
leads.why: The group goes over its minutes month after month, with about $20,000 spent year to date by June. Bill reminds the group, and Jill Chatterton reviews bills by hand and sets up each person's plan.

leads.work: Requests for trader IDs and Enpower desk access (Global Counterparty), plus other access requests and approvals
leads.why: Kate writes 'once again in need of a new trader ID'. Interns and new traders are missed and need follow-up, an 'Originator ID' is a further hurdle, and requests for directory access restrictions, schedule crawler removal and data-approver approvals all recur.

leads.work: Telephone and turret equipment requests: handsets, turret extensions, cabling and a Meridian phone
leads.why: Handsets keep going missing or getting damaged, and turret moves need repeated follow-up with IT.

leads.work: Manual reporting for service customers: Grays Harbor generator output reported to BPA, EES ancillary (spin) dispatch tracked in the service sheet and emailed to EES settlements, generation waiver notices, and Enron Canada coverage submitted by fax
leads.why: BPA says it will automate the Grays Harbor reporting, and Enron Canada submissions are faxed because there is no digital certificate. The rest is tracking sheets and emails kept by hand.

leads.work: Correcting Sitara deal prices and volumes for gas settlements (Guadalupe Power swing and baseload deals)
leads.why: There are repeated back-and-forth fixes, including a typed 50,000 that should have been 30,000, wrong prices and missing volume. One rate is computed by hand because Sitara can't handle the pricing formula.

leads.work: Researching counterparty payment disputes and missing or incorrect deals after the HPL sale to AEP (Killam, Conoco Big Cowboy about $1.5M a month overpaid, Coral, TUFCO actualized at 0, TGLO July deal)
leads.why: Megan Parker and others repeatedly ask Daren Farmer to find deals that are missing or wrong. They need investigation across Enron and AEP, and the records are poor.

leads.work: Manual intercompany booking for the Texas General Land Office gas-for-crude exchange (HPLC/ENA/EGM demand-fee deals each month)
leads.why: A multi-step monthly booking that was done for January and February but never finished for March onward, and a zeroed price was put back by someone else.

leads.work: Clearing prior-period pool balances (1999) and bridgeback errors, which need new transport deal tickets
leads.why: Volume Management chases deal tickets with emails and follow-ups going back two years, and late pathing causes bridgeback errors.

leads.work: Month-end disputes and book reallocations: the MPC March imbalance (5 months back and forth with tape requests) and the LP deal profit-share annuities explained again at month-end
leads.why: Long-running disputes and old deals have to be re-explained at every close.

leads.work: Administrative surveys and data checks: the OPM hours survey percentage split, the monthly admin assistant info check, and the month-end close schedule
leads.why: These recur monthly and are tracked by hand. The hours survey didn't prompt for the split, and the close schedule caused confusion.

leads.work: Expense report and approval notifications (Concur cellular expense approvals)
leads.why: Managers approve routine monthly cellular expense reports.

leads.work: Performance reviews, budgeting and staffing admin: PEP reviews and ranking communication, the 2002 G&A budget worksheet, interviews, job postings and training sign-ups
leads.why: Recurring HR and finance cycles handled through emailed spreadsheets and back-and-forth.

leads.work: CAISO adjustment bids for congestion (tiered bids entered by hand with error risk)
leads.why: Revenue was lost by not adjusting bids. A wrong tier entry forces flows at a loss, the CAISO system reads at most 10 bids, and traders are reminded repeatedly.

leads.work: Shift schedule changes and night discussion notes
leads.why: Shift swaps are communicated by email and hand-written on the schedule. Night notes are reviewed for completeness.

leads.work: System changes users must act on: ERMS RUNM migration, tie-line dialing change requiring auto-dial reprogramming, and Unify maintenance downtime coordination
leads.why: Each change is pushed to all users, who then have to act on it themselves.

leads.work: Weather info database/intranet for traders, maintained by hand
leads.why: Kate proposes a spreadsheet and web page that she would maintain herself. There is a possible overlap with a Fundamentals intranet being built separately.

leads.work: Gas nomination confirmations and origination materials (Pace Global nomination updates, market lists, team profiles)
leads.why: Nomination changes arrive as emailed spreadsheets 'until further notice'. Origination market lists are re-sorted and redistributed by hand.
